name: Ossic Resonance Baton ORB-3 'Earbreaker'
description:
The ORB-3 is a 60cm impact baton constructed from dense polymer composite over a titanium core, with a secondary function as a precision resonance delivery device. The baton's striking surface houses an array of micro-transducers capable of generating targeted ultrasonic pulses at the moment of contact, transmitting vibrational energy directly through struck surfaces — including bone, cartilage, and implant housings — rather than simply delivering blunt kinetic force. A standard impact from the ORB-3 carries the physical effect of the blow plus a concentrated resonance burst that propagates through the target's skeletal structure, inducing acute pain response, joint destabilization, and in repeated strikes, microfracture accumulation in bone density.

The weapon's resonance profile is tunable via a recessed dial at the base of the grip, allowing operators to shift between a bone-conduction pain mode, an inner-ear disruption mode that causes severe vertigo and nausea, and a structural mode intended for use against reinforced materials and door panels. The inner-ear mode is the weapon's most notorious application — a single strike to the shoulder or back of the head can induce complete vestibular disruption lasting between 30 seconds and several minutes, rendering a target unable to stand or orient without causing them any visible external injury.

Helix Biosystems developed the ORB-3 as a crowd-control tool for private security contracts, but the inner-ear mode was discovered and publicized by an independent weapons analyst within a year of launch. The subsequent controversy did not result in the weapon's prohibition but did generate a licensing requirement that is routinely circumvented through intermediary sales.
specifications:
length: 60cm
weight: 890g
core material: Titanium
shell material: Dense polymer composite
transducer array: 14-element contact surface
resonance profiles: 3
frequency range: 18,000–92,000 Hz (profile-dependent)
power source: Grip-integrated power cell, 3-hour continuous use
tuning interface: Recessed grip-base dial
tactical_use: Security personnel use the ORB-3 in crowd dispersal and suspect control scenarios where visible injury would create liability or media exposure. Inner-ear mode is applied via strikes to the upper back, shoulder, or base of the skull, and requires minimal accuracy to be effective. Bone-conduction pain mode is used in compliance and detention contexts. Structural mode sees use in breaching operations where a door panel or equipment housing needs to be compromised quickly and quietly. Experienced operators rotate between modes within a single engagement based on target response.
cultural_context: The ORB-3 has become a symbol of what activists in GLMZ call 'clean brutality' — enforcement violence that leaves no marks and therefore no evidence. Several civil rights organizations have campaigned unsuccessfully for its prohibition, and at least one advocacy group distributes inner-ear disruption countermeasures — small foam inserts that partially attenuate the resonance effect — in high-policing districts. Private security firms prize the weapon precisely because its effects are difficult to document, and the licensing requirement is widely seen as a formality that provides legal cover without meaningful restriction.
known_users: Organized crime enforcers operating in districts with active surveillance
story_hooks: A civil rights lawyer is building a case against a private security firm for the ORB-3 deaths of three protesters — but the deaths were officially attributed to pre-existing conditions, and the firm's contract specifically indemnifies them for resonance weapon use. She needs someone to find the security footage that was 'lost.'

A HELIX BIOSYSTEMS engineer who worked on the ORB-3's inner-ear mode has developed a modified version tuned specifically to disrupt a particular line of neural implants — and someone very powerful wants that modification before anyone else gets it.

An ORB-3 unit has been recovered from a crime scene with its resonance log showing a frequency sequence that exactly matches the vibrational signature of a specific building's structural resonance frequency. Someone was testing whether the weapon could be used at scale.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, purposeful impact baton with a subtly aggressive aesthetic—60cm of tapered polymer over titanium, culminating in a bulbous striking end densely clustered with micro-transducers. The grip flares slightly at the base, housing the tuning dial. Overall impression: a precision instrument disguised as blunt trauma, with an almost medical sterility to its finish.
physical_description.dimensions: 60cm length × 4.2cm grip diameter × 7cm striking head diameter
physical_description.weight_description: Hefty but balanced—890g distributes evenly along the shaft, making it feel authoritative in hand without excessive fatigue during extended use. The titanium core adds substantive presence without unwieldy bulk.
physical_description.primary_material: Titanium core wrapped in dense polymer composite shell
physical_description.finish: Matte gunmetal gray polymer with brushed titanium accents at the grip base and transducer array housing. Minor wear patterns consistent with field use.
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary: gunmetal gray polymer. Accents: brushed titanium silver at cap and grip collar. Recessed dial rim in muted copper tone.
physical_description.grip_texture: Rubberized polymer with subtle cross-hatching for secure hand purchase, slightly tacky to facilitate quick repositioning during strikes
distinctive_features: 14-element micro-transducer array visible as precision-drilled dimples across the 3cm striking surface
Recessed grip-base dial (copper-toned ring, labeled 1-3 in ultra-thin lettering for pain/vertigo/structural modes)
Tapered shaft with slight swelling toward striking end to house transducer power distribution
Helix Biosystems logo (interlocking DNA-like helix) stamped into grip collar
Small amber LED positioned in grip collar base (indicates power cell status—green when charged, amber when depleted)
Minimal air vents along grip shaft to manage heat dissipation during extended use
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: HELIX BIOSYSTEMS embossed on grip collar in clean sans-serif. Serial number etched into grip base beneath recessed dial. Faint regulatory licensing stamp on lower shaft (barely visible without close inspection).
physical_description.condition_typical: Well-maintained and field-ready. Polymer shows minimal scuffing; transducer array kept immaculate for optimal contact transmission. Operated by trained security personnel rather than street users, so cosmetic condition usually exceeds functional condition indicators.
